exposure: social support received by pregnant mothers
finding: A low Maternity Social Support Scale (MSSS) score was associated with a higher probability of stopping breastfeeding before 6 months of age and having a cesarean section, while a high MSSS score was associated with a lower likelihood of ceasing breastfeeding before 6 months and having a cesarean section.
mod_finding: A low MSSS score was associated with a higher probability of having a cesarean section and a lower probability of having a spontaneous labor and delivery, while a high MSSS score was associated with a lower likelihood of cesarean section and higher likelihood of spontaneous onset labor and delivery.
